items.summaryEn: Lando Norris qualified third for the Las Vegas Grand Prix with a 1m34.244s in Q3, 0.093 seconds behind inherited polesitter Max Verstappen and 0.020s behind George Russell, but afterwards called McLaren's MCL40 "awful in the straight."
detailZh: 诺里斯称迈凯伦MCL40直道表现糟糕，尽管他在拉斯维加斯大奖赛排位赛位列第三
诺里斯表示，尽管在拉斯维加斯大奖赛排位赛中获得第三，迈凯伦MCL40在直道上表现糟糕
致迈凯伦车迷。来自沃金的木瓜色新闻，带来车手、赛车、车队策略以及每个比赛周末的最新消息。
诺里斯将在2026年拉斯维加斯大奖赛从第三位发车，他在Q3跑出1分34秒244，仅落后继承杆位的维斯塔潘0.093秒，落后梅赛德斯的拉塞尔0.020秒。纸面上看，锁定第二排对迈凯伦而言像是一次不错的回升。然而诺里斯走出座舱后，给出了本赛季对MCL40最尖锐的批评之一。
诺里斯在排位赛中位列第四快，落后于被罚退的世界冠军基米·安东内利（1分33秒893），他坚称自己在Q3的最后一圈“显然是我最好的一圈”，但迈凯伦在1.9公里长直道上的极速劣势让他的努力付诸东流。
“我们在直道上简直糟透了，直道上太可怕了，所以我的圈速已经非常好了，”诺里斯说。“跟基米相比，我们在最后一个计时段慢了零点八秒。他有一个完美的尾流，他做得非常好，但跟大多数其他人相比，我们落后太多了。”
安东内利在后方直道上借助尾流获得了高达16公里/小时的提升，诺里斯解释说，为了追求类似的尾流，他被迫做出了严苛的妥协——在距离前车1.5秒的位置开始飞驰圈，而脏空气在每个弯角都剥夺了“至少零点零五到零点一秒”的圈速。“我们不得不弥补直道速度的严重损失，因此我们必须牺牲自己的过弯速度，”他补充道。
当被问及拉斯维加斯漫长的全油门路段是否只是放大了现有的缺陷时，诺里斯拒绝让这条赛道背锅。
诺里斯说：“不，我的意思是，你不能怪直道。只是我们的车不够好。我们必须在这方面大幅改进。你没法竞争。蒙扎、这里、巴库，我们表现糟糕，因为我们在直道上太差了，明年必须改进。”
迈凯伦2026赛季的成绩单印证了他的沮丧。诺里斯本赛季的三场胜利都来自高下压力赛道——匈牙利、赞德沃特和圣保罗——在这些地方，过弯负载比低阻力更重要。在动力敏感型布局上，木瓜色赛车一直难以竞争：在蒙扎，诺里斯从第八位发车，最终以第四名完赛，落后安东内利超过19秒；而在巴库，诺里斯退赛后，奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里以第13名完赛，迈凯伦一分未得。
这种直道上的脆弱性在周六晚间50圈的比赛前显得尤为突出。在制造商锦标赛中，迈凯伦落后红牛车队17分（415比398）排名第三，还剩三轮比赛，迈凯伦看到两辆红牛——维斯塔潘杆位、伊萨克·哈贾尔第四——正好排在诺里斯周围。
与此同时，皮亚斯特里以第7名（1分34秒899）排位，但在使用本赛季第五台内燃机后降至第17位。即便从第三位发车，诺里斯也必须奋力拼搏才能守住赛道位置，对手包括从第六位冲锋的安东内利等直道更快的车手。
detailEn: Lando Norris brands McLaren “awful in the straight” despite third on Las Vegas GP grid
Lando Norris says McLaren's MCL40 is "awful in the straight" despite qualifying for third on the Las Vegas GP grid
For McLaren fans. Papaya news from Woking, with the latest on the drivers, the car, team strategy and every race weekend.

Lando Norris will launch from third on the grid for the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix after setting a 1m34.244s in Q3 - just 0.093 seconds shy of inherited polesitter Max Verstappen and 0.020s behind Mercedes’ George Russell. On paper, locking down the second row looks like a tidy recovery for McLaren. Yet Norris stepped out of the cockpit delivering one of his sharpest criticisms of the MCL40 all season.

Qualifying fourth fastest behind penalised world champion Kimi Antonelli (1m33.893s), Norris insisted his final Q3 effort was "easily my best lap," only for McLaren’s top-speed deficit to undo his work down the 1.9-kilometre Strip straight.

"We’re just shocking in the straights, like horrendous in the straight, so my lap was very good," Norris said. "To Kimi, we’re eight tenths off in the last sector. He has a perfect tow, and he does a very good job, but comparing to most other people, we’re too far off."

Antonelli’s slipstream down the back straight proved worth up to 16 km/h, and Norris explained that chasing a similar tow forced him into a punishing compromise - starting his lap 1.5s behind the car ahead while dirty air stripped away "at least a half a tenth to a tenth" in every corner. "We’re having to make up for a pretty terrible loss of straight-line speed, and therefore we have to harm our cornering speed," he added.
Asked whether Las Vegas’s long flat-out run simply exaggerated an existing flaw, Norris refused to let the circuit take the blame.

"No, I mean you can’t blame the straights. It’s just our car is not good. We have to improve that a lot," Norris said. "You cannot fight. Monza, here, Baku, we’re bad because we’re awful in the straight, and we have to improve for next year."

McLaren’s 2026 scorecard supports his frustration. All three of Norris’s wins this season came at higher-downforce venues - Hungary, Zandvoort, and São Paulo - where cornering load matters more than low drag. On power-sensitive layouts, the papaya cars have struggled to contend: at Monza, Norris started eighth and finished fourth more than 19s behind Antonelli, while Baku ended without a single point for McLaren after Norris retired and Oscar Piastri came home 13th.

That straight-line vulnerability looms large over Saturday night’s 50-lap race. Trailing Red Bull Racing by 17 points for third in the constructors’ championship (415 to 398) with three rounds remaining, McLaren sees both Red Bulls - Verstappen on pole and Isack Hadjar in fourth - lined up right around Norris.

Meanwhile, Piastri qualified seventh (1m34.899s) but drops to 17th after taking his fifth internal combustion engine of the year. Even starting third, Norris will have to fight hard just to defend track position against faster straight-line rivals, including Antonelli charging from sixth.

“一旦你失去了赛道位置，那对你不利。如果你是乔治，你被超越了，这是练习赛。好吧，你拿不回来，你失去了位置，继续前进。”
“那是一个完全没有必要的风险。你不想和马克斯成为敌人。”
回顾红牛车队的马克斯·维斯塔潘与梅赛德斯车队的乔治·拉塞尔之间一些最激烈的交锋。

“我们知道乔治永远不会向马克斯让步。我认为马克斯确实会尝试在这种事情上碰运气，这就是为什么他能够让自己处于有利位置。这也来自维修区墙上的指令，他们告诉他要穿过车流，奋力争取干净空气，他很有侵略性，确实会把别人挤开。大多数人都会对此让步，然后像利亚姆·劳森（在墨西哥城大奖赛）这样的人出现，不让步，结果惹上了大车队的麻烦。”
“我挺喜欢乔治对抗他这一点，因为马克斯是故意这么做的，他就是那样驾驶的。对此有值得肯定的一面，但也有需要抗争的一面。”

detailEn: George Russell hits out at Max Verstappen after Las Vegas GP clash and says 'somebody's got to stand up to that guy'

Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Mercedes' George Russell to start on front row of Las Vegas grid; Russell hit out at Verstappen after final practice collision; watch Sunday's race at 4am (build-up from 2.30am), live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event
George Russell reacted to the collision with Max Verstappen in final practice at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, accusing the Red Bull driver of of 'screwing' his rivals over

George Russell launched a scathing criticism of Max Verstappen after a collision between the pair in final practice at the Las Vegas Grand Prix ahead of a race they will now start on the front row together.
​​​The pair, who have had run-ins in the past on track in recent years, clashed wheels in final practice as they fought over track position.
Verstappen first overtook Russell on the run down The Strip to Turn 14 before the Mercedes went back down the inside of the Red Bull in the braking zone, with the two cars brushing wheels.

Stewards investigated the incident and issued a warning to Verstappen, ruling he had been "driving erratically" under braking into the corner once ahead of the Mercedes.

The pair went on to qualify second and third, which becomes first and second on the grid for Sunday's race at 4am, live on Sky Sports F1, due to Q3 pacesetter Kimi Antonelli's five-place grid penalty.
George Russell and Max Verstappen collided with one another during final practice at the Las Vegas Grand Prix
Asked after qualifying about the sanction issued to Verstappen by stewards, Russell said "a warning was fine" before going on to issue a withering rebuke of his Red Bull rival's approach.

Russell told Sky Italy: "There's nothing in the rules to say you cannot overtake someone who is starting a lap but when you do this, you are screwing this person over and he does this week in, week out with many drivers and everybody accepts it.
"I'm not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they're bigger and better than everyone else. Somebody's got to stand up to that guy."
Russell's comments about wanting to "stand up to" Verstappen echoed those he made following an incident in qualifying at the 2024 Qatar Grand Prix.

The pair traded barbs in person and via interviews after that clash, when Verstappen was given a one-place grid drop for impeding Russell in Q3, with the Mercedes driver then launching an explosive attack on his rival ahead of the following week's race in Abu Dhabi.
Back in 2024, Craig Slater took a closer look at how the Qatar penalty fallout escalated between George Russell and Max Verstappen

On Saturday, the pair were both asked when sitting next to each other in the post-qualifying press conference about the final practice incident and whether there had any confusion about the 'gentleman's agreement' regarding not disturbing a rival who was about to start a flying lap.
Verstappen said "nothing happened", while Russell said there was "no confusion, I think it was pretty clear".
What did the pundits make of the clash and Russell's comments?
Sky Sports F1's Jacques Villeneuve said of the incident itself: "Fun and exciting to watch! But we want to see this in the race, not in free practice. Unnecessary.
"Once you've lost your track position, too bad for you. If you're George, you got overtaken, it's practice. OK, you don't get it back, you lost your position and move on.
"That was a completely unnecessary risk. You don't want to make an enemy of Max."
A look back at some of the most heated clashes between Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Mercedes' George Russell
Speaking after hearing Russell's post-qualifying comments, Sky Sports F1's Jamie Chadwick said: "George saying he'll stand up to Max, I like that. It's very reminiscent of what we saw in Qatar.

"With George we know he's never going to give to Max. I think Max does try his luck with that kind of thing and that is why he is able to find himself in good positions. It comes also from the pit wall, who are telling him to push through the traffic and fight his way to get clear air, and he's aggressive and he does bully people out of the way. Most people do give in to that and then someone like Liam Lawson [at the Mexico City GP] comes along, doesn't, and gets in trouble from the big team.

"I quite like the fact that George is standing up to him because Max does it intentionally, he drives like that. There is something good to be said for that, but there's also something that needs to be fought against."
Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix

With the pair now starting together on the front row for the short run to Las Vegas' first corner, Villeneuve added: "No love lost there, so that's good before the start for tomorrow! That will make it exciting.

"He shouldn't overtake someone who is about to start his lap, true, but how does that person know you're about to start your lap? That's one thing, and maybe you're about to start your own lap yourself.
"So that's a difficult one to judge, ultimately."

这对车手在FP3的最后一圈在14号弯道发生了接触，当时拉塞尔在内线试图重新超越红牛车队。 stewards在发现维斯塔潘在刹车时的方向改变不可预测后，对他进行了警告。
stewards认为3号车的刹车时方向改变不可预测，并导致了63号车为了避免碰撞而不得不内移的情况。官方FIA文件解释说。
虽然 stewards认为这个动作并不严重到需要更严厉的处罚，但他们得出结论，在这种情况下刹车时的方向改变低于预期的驾驶标准。
在拉斯维加斯大道的排位赛后，拉塞尔在接受天空体育采访时谈到了FP3的事故。他说：“我不会就这样接受有人这样对我，然后像他们比所有人都大或更好一样四处走动。有人必须站出来对抗那个人。”

拉塞尔在拉斯维加斯大奖赛中获得第三名，排在队友安东内利和维斯塔潘之后，但意大利车手的引擎处罚意味着维斯塔潘和拉塞尔将分别从第一和第二位发车。

detailEn: Max Verstappen dismisses George Russell Las Vegas clash with two-word response
Verstappen and Russell will start first and second after Kimi Antonelli’s engine penalty
For Red Bull fans. Keeping watch on Red Bull Racing, with F1 news, driver updates, technical insight and race analysis from Milton Keynes.
Four-time Formula 1 champion Max Verstappen dismissed his final practice clash with George Russell in two words after qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix: "Nothing happened."

The pair made contact at Turn 14 at the end of FP3, when Russell went down the inside to re-pass the Red Bull. The stewards gave Verstappen a warning for erratic driving after finding that his change of direction under braking was "unpredictable".

"The Stewards considered that Car 3's change of direction under braking was unpredictable and contributed to the situation in which Car 63 had to move to the inside to avoid contact," the official FIA document explained.

"While the Stewards did not consider the manoeuvre sufficiently serious to warrant a more severe penalty, they concluded that changing direction under braking in these circumstances fell below the standard of driving expected."

While speaking to Sky Sports after qualifying on the Las Vegas Strip, Russell commented on the FP3 incident. "I'm not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they're bigger and better than everyone else," he said. "Somebody's got to stand up to that guy."
Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing

Russell qualified third for the Las Vegas Grand Prix behind his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli and Verstappen, but an engine penalty for the Italian driver means Verstappen and Russell will start first and second.
Verstappen was asked about the FP3 clash in the post-qualifying press conference following Russell's comments. "Nothing happened," he answered simply.

Both Verstappen and Russell are currently fighting for second in the drivers' championship. With three rounds remaining in 2026, Verstappen is second with 279 points and Russell is third with 262 points. Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton is just one point behind Russell in fourth.
The Las Vegas Grand Prix kicks off the season-ending triple-header, which includes the Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix.

items.titleZh: 法拉利拉斯维加斯排位赛双车无缘Q3
items.summaryZh: 法拉利在拉斯维加斯排位赛中两位车手均未能进入Q3，创下本赛季最差排位赛表现。勒克莱尔因7号弯失误中止Q2第二圈，最终排名第11（因皮亚斯特里罚退从第10位起步），汉密尔顿则受能量部署问题和Q1车损影响。
items.originalTitle: What explains Ferrari’s worst F1 2026 qualifying
items.summaryEn: Neither Ferrari driver made it into Q3 in Las Vegas qualifying, marking the team's worst qualifying showing of the Formula 1 season so far. Charles Leclerc aborted his second Q2 run after a mistake at Turn 7 and ended up 11th fastest (starting 10th thanks to Oscar Piastri's penalty), while Lewis Hamilton right behind him was hampered by deployment problems and car damage picked up in Q1.
detailZh: 法拉利原本预计在拉斯维加斯的长直道上会很艰难，但两位车手都未能进入Q3，这标志着其本赛季至今最差的排位赛表现。
夏尔·勒克莱尔在7号弯出现失误后被迫中止Q2第二圈，就此断送机会。他最终排名第11快（因奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里受罚，他从第10位起步），紧随其后的刘易斯·汉密尔顿则受到能量部署问题和Q1中车损的影响。
但法拉利的问题要深得多，因为极速不足叠加车手在排位赛中让轮胎升温的持续难题，共同决定了他们的命运。
而且，正如勒克莱尔在排位赛后接受媒体采访时公开承认的那样，他在7号弯的失误源于对速度不足的日益不满以及与维修区持续存在的沟通问题。
“我认为这是在一连串挫败之后发生的，我们在管理一切、交通和其他事情上犯了很多错误，这些错误不断累积，”他解释道。
“这没有帮助，尤其是在这样一条一切都取决于轮胎的赛道上。你必须把轮胎带入正确的工作窗口。
“我更多是在看后视镜，试图自己弄明白交通状况，这让人很难做任何事。”
法拉利众所周知的动力单元弱点在拉斯维加斯尤其代价高昂。
“我只是非常失望，”他说。“我们原本有所期待，但在直道上损失了一秒——这太疯狂了。这是意料之中的，而这让事情变得非常、非常困难。
“在这样的赛道上，这是本赛季对动力最敏感的赛道，所以我们预料到会很艰难。但我原本期望能进入第三节排位赛（Q3）。”
汉密尔顿表示，法拉利并非没有意识到拉斯维加斯是一个更具挑战性的周末，但他也认同结果比预期更糟。
“我们知道长直道之类的东西会很有挑战性，但在直道上的差距似乎比我预期的要大一些，”他说。
“这并非无关紧要。在直道上损失很大。然后我不知道，就抓地力而言，感觉我们并没有很强的抓地力。我们很难让轮胎进入工作状态，而且我们就是有点找不到方向。”
然而，汉密尔顿觉得，尽管存在轮胎和极速问题，但考虑到损伤带来的空气动力学损失和能量管理问题，赛车仍有潜力进入Q3。
“我们在Q1的第一圈或第二圈损失了一块底板。赛车平衡发生了变化，我们损失了百分之三到四秒（积分）的下压力，”他说。“在那之后，我们更多是在打滑中挣扎，基本上从一开始就是这样。
“我最后那一圈真的很好，但我用现有的条件做到了最好。但后来我们在部署上损失了大约百分之六秒。我想如果没有那个损失，我们本可以进入Q3。但除此之外，我对我的圈速很满意。”
还有更多执行层面的问题吗？
另一个受到关注的方面是车队如何执行排位赛，因为法拉利在赛道位置上陷入挣扎，并且没有选择像许多其他车队那样玩尾流游戏。
勒克莱尔表示，法拉利没有走那条路线，是因为考虑到今年在轮胎管理上挣扎的程度，它不认为一个好的尾流能带来接近让轮胎处于完美工作窗口内的好处。
“我的意思是，那并没有被讨论过，”他说。“我们认为轮胎就是一切。保持轮胎温度对我们来说是最重要的。”
“我们知道这是我们的弱点。我们必须推进。即使在冷却圈，我们也必须推进以保持轮胎高温。
“我不知道其他人是否面临和我们一样的问题，但当你遇到那个问题时，就很难等两辆车，并把握好时机，因为那需要你开得比你能开的更慢。对我们来说，保持那些轮胎的温度非常非常棘手。”
交通管理方面也再次出现了沟通问题，但勒克莱尔想更好地了解车队在练习中遇到的GPS问题是否在排位赛中造成了困难。
“我不知道今天的原因是什么，”他说。“我知道今天早上我们在GPS上有很多问题。如果今天那是问题，那就可以理解。”
“否则，我们只需要确保在那些关键时刻把一切做对。”
他补充道：“如果是GPS问题，那不一定来自我们，那就是我们无能为力的事情，今天很痛苦。”
“但如果问题来自我们，我确实同意我们需要审视它并显然加以改进，因为特别是在这样的关键时刻，我们需要在场，而我们没有做到。”
detailEn: Ferrari braced for a tough time on the long straights of Las Vegas, but neither driver making it into Q3 marked its worst qualifying showing of the Formula 1 season so far.

Charles Leclerc had wrecked his chances when he was forced to abort his second Q2 run after a mistake at Turn 7. He ended up 11th fastest (he starts 10th thanks to Oscar Piastri's penalty), while right behind him Lewis Hamilton was not helped by deployment problems and some car damage that he picked up in Q1.

But Ferrari’s problems ran much deeper because a combination of its lack of top speed allied to the ongoing issues its drivers have faced in firing tyres up for qualifying that consigned them to their fate.

And, as Leclerc openly admitted when he spoke to the media after qualifying, the error he made in T7 was a consequence of growing annoyance at the lack of pace and ongoing communication problems with the pit wall.
“I think that is following a lot of frustration, building up with a lot of mistakes with the way we managed everything, traffic and other things,” he explained.
“That doesn't help, particularly on a track like this where it's all about tyres. You've got to put tyres in the right window.
“I was more looking in my mirrors and trying to understand the traffic myself, that it makes it very difficult to do anything.”
Ferrari's well-known power unit weakness was particularly costly in Vegas.
“I'm just very disappointed,” he said. “We were expecting, and we lost one second down the straight - which is crazy. It's expected, and that makes it very, very difficult.
“On a track like this, it's the most power-sensitive track of the season, so we expected to have a hard time. But I was expecting to go through Q3.”
Hamilton said Ferrari wasn't blind to Las Vegas being a more challenging weekend, but he agreed the outcome was worse than anticipated.
“We knew long straights and stuff was going to be challenging, but the gap seems to be a little bit more than I anticipated in the straightline,” he said.

“It's not insignificant. It's a big chunk on the straights. And then I don't know, just grip-wise, it didn't feel like we had a tonne of grip. We were struggling to get the tyres working and we were just kind of nowhere."

Hamilton felt, however, that even in spite of the tyre and top speed problems, the potential was still within the car to make it to Q3 – taking into account the aero deficit from damage and energy management issues.

“We lost a piece of the floor on the first or second lap of Q1. The car balance shifted and we lost three or four tenths [points] of downforce,” he said. “After that we were struggling more so with sliding, basically from the get-go.

“My lap was really good at the end, but I did the best I could with what I had. But then we lost something like six tenths just in deployment. I think without that we would have been in Q3. But otherwise, I was happy with my lap.”
More execution problems?
Another element that came under the spotlight was how the team executed qualifying, as Ferrari struggled for track position and didn't elect to play the slipstream game that many others were doing.

Leclerc said that Ferrari had not gone down that route because it did not think a good tow would offer anywhere near the benefits of having tyres in the perfect operating window, considering how much it has struggled this year in managing its rubber.
“I mean, that was not discussed,” he said. “We thought that tyres were just everything. Keeping just the temperature in the tyres was the most important for us.
“We know it's our weakness. We've got to push. Even in the cool-down laps, we've got to push to keep the tyres high.

“I don't know if the others are facing the same issues as we do, but when you have that problem, then it's very difficult to wait for two cars, and to time it well, because that requires you to go slower than what you can. It's very, very tricky for us to keep those tyres up.”

There were also communication problems again with traffic management, but Leclerc wanted to understand better if GPS problems the team had suffered in practice had played a part in making things difficult in qualifying.
“I don't know what was the reason for that today,” he said. “I know this morning we had a lot of problems on GPS. If that was a problem today, then it's understandable.
“Otherwise, we just need to make sure that in those critical moments we get everything right.
He added: “If it's a GPS issue, which doesn't necessarily come from us, then it's something that we cannot do much, and today was painful.
"But if it comes from us, I do agree we need to look at it and obviously improve, because particularly in the critical moments like this, we need to be there, and we didn't.”

detailZh: 维斯塔潘回应乔治·拉塞尔在拉斯维加斯碰撞事件
维斯塔潘表示，他没有打算在拉斯维加斯F1第三场练习赛中浪费时间去处理与拉塞尔的这次事件
在F1拉斯维加斯大奖赛的最后一场练习赛中，维斯塔潘和乔治·拉塞尔再次相遇。荷兰人超越了梅赛德斯车手，但随后在拉塞尔面前减速，据裁判长所说，他还多次改变方向
随后，拉塞尔从四次世界冠军的内侧超车，导致两人在14号弯发生接触。这使两位对手都受到了裁判长的调查，尽管他们最终通过发出警告来处理了这次事件。与斥责不同，警告没有任何后果
当被问及在排位赛后的新闻发布会上发生的意外时，维斯塔潘对讨论此事兴趣不大。当被问及发生了什么，他简单地回答道：“没什么。什么都没发生。”
然而，拉塞尔随后在媒体区对红牛车手发起了猛烈的抨击。在接受天空体育意大利采访时，拉塞尔表示，其中之一是：
“我不会接受有人这样背叛我，然后像他们比所有人都大更好一样四处走动。有人必须站出来对抗那个人。”
维斯塔潘在很大程度上不为所动。当Motorsport.com在拉斯维加斯赛道区的荷兰媒体会上问他关于碰撞时，他回答道：
“我甚至不想在这方面浪费时间。这对我的意义根本不大。”
当有人指出 stewards 在 FIA 文档中提到了准备圈中的绅士协议，即在开始飞驰圈之前，车手们应保持自己的位置并避免相互干扰，维斯塔潘回应说：“我一生中从未见过这样的协议。”
stewards 还明确表示，他们在做出决定时对 拉塞尔 提到的绅士协议重视程度不高，而是专注于两位车手的行动。
stewards 记录了这些解释，但认为这种非正式的理解对评估事件的相关性有限。决定性因素是两辆车的实际移动和它们相对的位置。
特别值得注意的是，由于基米·安东内利的发车罚分，两位车手将在周六晚上的拉斯维加斯赛道占据发车区的第一排，但维斯塔潘坚称这次碰撞并没有给他任何额外的动力来保持对拉塞尔的领先。
不，那绝对不是我获得动力的地方。
detailEn: Max Verstappen responds to George Russell after Vegas clash
Verstappen says he has no intention of wasting his time on the incident with Russell during F1’s third practice session in Las Vegas

During the final practice session for the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix, Max Verstappen and George Russell crossed paths once again. The Dutchman overtook the Mercedes driver, but then slowed down in front of him and, according to the stewards, changed direction several times.

Russell subsequently went down the inside of the four-time world champion, leading to contact between the two at Turn 14. It earned both rivals a trip to the stewards, although they ultimately dealt with the incident by issuing a warning. Unlike a reprimand, a warning carries no consequences at all.

When Verstappen was asked about the incident during the press conference after qualifying, the Dutchman had little interest in discussing it. Asked what had happened, he simply replied: "Nothing. Nothing happened."
Russell, however, subsequently launched a scathing attack on the Red Bull driver in the media pen. Speaking to Sky Sports Italy, Russell said, among other things:
"I’m not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they’re bigger and better than everyone else. Somebody has got to stand up to that guy."
Verstappen was largely unmoved. When Motorsport.com asked him about the clash during the Dutch media session that followed in the Las Vegas paddock, he replied:
"I don't even want to waste my time on that. It's not worth it to me at all."

When it was pointed out that the stewards had referred in the FIA document to a gentlemen's agreement during preparation laps, under which drivers are expected to maintain their positions and avoid interfering with one another before starting a flying lap, Verstappen responded: "I've never seen such an agreement in my life."
The stewards also made clear that they had attached little weight to the gentlemen's agreement mentioned by Russell in reaching their decision, instead focusing on the actions of both drivers.

"The Stewards noted these explanations but considered that such informal understandings were of limited relevance to the assessment of the incident. The decisive considerations were the actual movements of both cars and their relative positions."

It is particularly notable that the two drivers will share the front row of the grid in Vegas on Saturday night following Kimi Antonelli's grid penalty, but Verstappen insists the clash has not given him any extra motivation to keep Russell behind.
"No, that's definitely not where I get my motivation from."

items.summaryEn: Both Ferraris failed to make it out of Q2 in qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix, with Lewis Hamilton attributing the exit to energy deployment and floor damage.
detailZh: 汉密尔顿揭示法拉利F1赛车在拉斯维加斯排位赛Q2出局后的损伤
法拉利两位车手在拉斯维加斯大奖赛排位赛中表现不佳，均未能晋级Q3
汉密尔顿将法拉利在拉斯维加斯大奖赛排位赛中的Q2出局归因于能量部署和底板损伤，这位七届世界冠军觉得自己已经从整体轮胎抓地力的困难中恢复过来。
这位英国车手在第三节练习中刹车时全程挣扎，前轮特别容易锁死，导致汉密尔顿多次冲出赛道进入缓冲区。
汉密尔顿在排位赛首节虽然底板受损，但仍闯入了Q2，不过他和夏尔·勒克莱尔都未能进入争夺杆位的前十名淘汰赛。
汉密尔顿在Q2的飞驰圈中总体显得满意，这些圈速很少出现他在排位赛前常见的锁死轮胎现象，但法拉利动力单元的能量部署似乎比梅赛德斯和红牛动力赛车更早达到极限，抑制了直线性能。
法拉利在动力上一直落后于这两家制造商，而拉斯维加斯大道沿线的长加速区在整个练习与排位赛节次中暴露了这一劣势。
“我们在Q1的第一圈或第二圈损失了一块底板，赛车平衡发生了变化，我想我们损失了大约三到四成的下压力，”汉密尔顿表示。
“而在那之后，我们更多是在打滑方面挣扎，但基本上从一开始就是这样。”
“然后我的最后一圈在结尾时真的很好，但我用现有的条件做到了最好。但后来我们仅仅在部署上就损失了大约零点六秒。所以我认为有了那个我们本可以进入Q3，但除此之外我对自己的圈速感到满意。”
“我们知道长直道之类的东西会很有挑战性。差距在直线上似乎比我预想的要大一点。这并非微不足道。在直道上是一个很大的部分。”
一直有一种普遍的感觉，认为法拉利会在拉斯维加斯的低温条件下挣扎，因为该车队在整个2026赛季都难以在排位圈中保持轮胎温度。
汉密尔顿也认为这辆赛车很难驾驭，在低速弯中频繁打滑，尤其是在损失了一部分底板之后，他只希望法拉利能在周六晚上的正赛中有所进步，因为车队的目标是锁定制造商年度亚军。
“就抓地力而言，感觉我们并没有很强的抓地力。我们一直很难让轮胎进入工作状态，就是有点找不到感觉，”他补充道。
“今年这些轮胎非常非常难进入工作状态，即使在高温路面上也是如此。所以这确实很困难。我对正赛没有任何期待。只是想看看自己能不能往前赶。”
detailEn: Lewis Hamilton reveals Ferrari F1 car damage after Las Vegas Q2 exit
Both Ferraris failed to make the cut for Q3 after floundering in qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix

Lewis Hamilton put Ferrari's Q2 exit in qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix down to energy deployment and floor damage, as the seven-time champion felt he'd rallied from difficulties with overall tyre grip.
The Briton struggled throughout FP3 under braking, as the front tyres proved particularly lock-up prone and resulted in Hamilton enduring multiple excursions into the run-off.
Hamilton landed in Q2 despite suffering floor damage in the opening stage of qualifying, but neither he nor Charles Leclerc were able to make their way into the top-10 shootout for pole.

Hamilton appeared generally happy with his runs in Q2, which demonstrated few of the lock-ups characteristic of his lead-up to qualifying, but the Ferrari power unit's energy deployment seemed to hit its maximum sooner than the Mercedes and Red Bull-powered cars and inhibited straightline performance.
Ferrari has been down on power versus those two manufacturers, and the long acceleration zone along the Strip exposed this deficit throughout the session.
"We lost a piece of the floor on the first or second lap of Q1 and the car balance shifted, and we lost I think it was like three or four tenths of downforce we lost," Hamilton stated.
"And then after that we were struggling more so with sliding, but it was basically from the get-go.

"And then my last lap was really good at the end, but I did the best I could with what I had. But then we lost something like six tenths just on deployment. So I think with that we would have been in Q3, but otherwise I was happy with my lap.
"We knew long straights and stuff was going to be challenging. The gap seems to be a little bit more than I anticipated in a straight line. It's not insignificant. It's a big chunk on the straights.

There had been a pervading sense that Ferrari would struggle in the low-temperature conditions in Las Vegas, as the team has struggled throughout 2026 to maintain tyre temperature through a qualifying lap.

Hamilton agreed that the car was difficult to work with amid frequent sliding through the low-speed corners, especially after losing a chunk of floor, and only hopes that Ferrari can move forward in the Saturday night race as it aims to lock out second in the constructors' championship.
"Just grip-wise, it just didn't feel like we had a ton of grip. We were struggling to get the tyres working and we were just kind of nowhere," he added.

"These tyres have been very, very difficult this year to get working, even on hot surfaces. So it's definitely been difficult. I don't have any expectations [for the race]. Just trying to see if I can move forward."

Both Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc were eliminated from Q2 as Ferrari were left frustrated in Las Vegas qualifying
Charles Leclerc was left "angry" while Lewis Hamilton said he was "devastated" after both Ferrari drivers suffered shock early exits from Las Vegas Grand Prix Qualifying.

The Italian team had arrived at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit wary of the challenges the long straights and cold temperatures could pose them, but Friday night's session went far worse than either driver had anticipated.
Both drivers were eliminated in Q2 as Leclerc took 11th with Hamilton a place behind him. They will each move a position forward on the grid due to a penalty for McLaren's Oscar Piastri.

"And at the same time, the execution has been very poor. I don't know. We'll review.

'Devastated' Hamilton reveals damage and deployment issues
Hamilton was lacking pace throughout the session, which he suggested was caused by damage he had done to his car in the early stages.
"I'm devastated," Hamilton told Sky Sports F1. "We work hard to do a good job.
"I didn't really know where we were going to be today. We knew we would struggle a little bit with these long straights, but I was optimistic going in, I thought the car would be OK.
"But on the first or second lap, we took a hit from something on the floor, some debris or something damaged the floor and we lost a bunch of downforce with it, a few tenths."

Unlike Leclerc, Hamilton was able to get a flying lap in at the end of Q2, but he said a deployment issue all but ended his hopes of advancing.

"And then I was giving it everything," he added. "My lap was as good as it could be at the end, but I didn't have anyone ahead of me, and then we had a lack of deployment at the end and I lost like six tenths just on deployment.

"We were scrapping to just get into Q3. I think without the deployment loss, without the downforce loss, I think I could have got into Q3, but it would have still been tough.
"But it is what is, it's over. It's definitely not a nice feeling for all the team, but we'll try to move forwards tomorrow."

detailEn: Isack Hadjar: Red Bull "looked a bit stupid" in Vegas qualifying tow game
The Red Bull driver says rival teams outsmarted him on the final run, but he believes starting fourth leaves him "in a good position for a podium"
For Red Bull fans. Keeping watch on Red Bull Racing, with F1 news, driver updates, technical insight and race analysis from Milton Keynes.

Isack Hadjar has admitted that Red Bull "looked a bit stupid" in what became a tow battle at the end of Las Vegas Grand Prix qualifying. He says it "doesn't really matter" where he starts on Saturday night.
Hadjar set the fifth-fastest time in Q3, 0.699s behind Kimi Antonelli, while team-mate Max Verstappen took pole after the Italian's five-place grid penalty. Hadjar moves up to fourth on the grid.

The final runs in Q3 turned into a game of cat and mouse, as drivers attempted to position themselves in the tow of other drivers down the long straights of the Vegas circuit. While many achieved, Hadjar was left to rely on only his Ford power unit.
"No, we had no tow. So yeah, we looked a bit stupid out there for the final run, but the other teams played it very smart, parking the car in Turn 1 while we were exiting the pit," Hadjar said.
With nobody ahead of him, Hadjar said a good lap would have unraveled regardless with no tow on the straights, so he decided to abort.
Asked whether Red Bull would play those games better next time, he admitted he'd rather just race and not rely on the gamble of such a scenario.
"Yeah, I don't really like those games anyway. I like driving the car fast," he said. "There's just things you can't really control, and it's a bit like rolling the dice."
"Yeah, so I don't really care. As long as I know I was quick around the corners, I'm happy about that. And in the end, we're starting fourth tomorrow, so we're in a good position for a podium."
Hadjar was confident he had the pace to fight at the front, saying "I am definitely up there".

"Job done on my side, and then I think it's a track where you can easily overtake with these massive straights and with the current regulations. So P4, P5, P2, it doesn't really matter in the end, so I'm happy," he said.
Hadjar has three podiums in his first season with Red Bull, at Monaco, Azerbaijan and Sao Paulo, where he finished third behind Lando Norris and Verstappen.
Another would be welcome for Red Bull, which is fighting for second in the constructors' championship and just 17 points ahead of McLaren, with just three races to go.

detailZh: 拉塞尔：拉斯维加斯排位赛尾流"太难协调"
拉塞尔排位赛位列第三，但安东内利的罚退使他升至第二位，与马克斯·维斯塔潘同排发车
致梅赛德斯车迷。来自银箭车队的最新消息，包括F1新闻、车手动态、赛车研发以及来自布拉克利和布里克斯沃思的赛事分析。
梅赛德斯F1车手乔治·拉塞尔在错失杆位后表示，在拉斯维加斯排位赛中要获得完美的尾流"太难协调"。
拉塞尔在Q3中跑出第三快的时间，落后队友基米·安东内利0.331秒，落后红牛的马克斯·维斯塔潘0.073秒。由于安东内利因动力单元更换被罚退五位，他将与维斯塔潘并排从第二位发车。
在拉斯维加斯大道的高速直道上，尾流效应价值巨大。考虑到安东内利已被处以引擎罚单并在墨西哥赢得了车手总冠军，拉塞尔在排位赛最后一圈前一直在询问能否从队友那里获得尾流牵引。
但当所有人涌出维修区时，最终受益于尾流的却是这位意大利车手，而非拉塞尔。
当天空体育询问梅赛德斯的计划是否奏效时，拉塞尔表示：“这太难协调了，要获得完美的尾流风险极高。”
马克斯·维斯塔潘，红牛车队，乔治·拉塞尔，梅赛德斯
“基米，如果他晚一秒开始飞驰圈，根本跑不完一圈，而最终他在直道上赚回了一秒，甚至更多，可能在弯道里丢了六成。所以这简直难以置信。
“整体影响而言，我对这节练习仍然非常满意，因为今天每一圈或整个周末，我都相当有竞争力。”
谈到最后一轮飞驰圈混乱的开局，这位英国车手补充道：“两次在队首离开维修区时我都非常紧张。但当有些车手做预热圈、另一些车手直接冲刺时，这太难协调了。每个人都在找尾流。”
“现在有点墨西哥对峙的意味。所以最终来说，这是高风险、高回报。明天从第一排发车，我们已经连续三场比赛都处在第一排了。所以这还不错。”
2026赛季还剩三站，拉塞尔目前位列车手积分榜第三，落后第二名维斯塔潘17分，仅领先第四名法拉利车手汉密尔顿1分。
detailEn: George Russell: Las Vegas qualifying tow was "too difficult to orchestrate"
George Russell qualified third, but Kimi Antonelli's penalty promotes him to second alongside Max Verstappen
For Mercedes fans. All the latest from the Silver Arrows, with F1 news, driver updates, car development and race analysis from Brackley and Brixworth.
Mercedes Formula 1 driver George Russell claimed that getting the perfect tow in Las Vegas qualifying was "too difficult to orchestrate" after he missed out on pole position.

Russell set the third-fastest time in Q3, 0.331 seconds behind team-mate Kimi Antonelli and 0.073s off Red Bull's Max Verstappen. He will start second, alongside Verstappen, after Antonelli's five-place grid penalty for power unit changes.

A slipstream is worth a huge amount on the long straights of the Las Vegas Strip. Taking into account that Antonelli has been handed an engine penalty and won the drivers' championship in Mexico, Russell had been asking about getting a tow from his team-mate on his final run in qualifying.
But as everyone piled out of the pits, the Italian driver ended up being the one to benefit from a tow rather than Russell.
Asked by Sky Sports whether Mercedes' plans had worked, Russell said: "It was so difficult to orchestrate and getting the perfect tow is high risk.
Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes
"Kimi, if he started his lap a second later, wouldn't have gone a lap in and in the end, he gained a second on the straight, maybe more and maybe lost six tenths in the corners. So it's unbelievable.
"The impact overall, I'm still very pleased with the session because every lap today or this whole weekend, I've been pretty competitive."

Addressing the chaotic start to the final flying laps, the Briton added: "I was very nervous when I left the pits on both occasions at the front of the pack. But it's too difficult to orchestrate when you've got some drivers doing a prep lap, other drivers going straight for it. Everyone's going for a tow.
"There's a bit of a Mexican standoff. So in the end, it's high-risk, high-reward. And starting on the front row tomorrow, three races in a row we've been on the front row. So that's all right."

With three rounds remaining in the 2026 season, Russell currently sits third in the drivers' championship, 17 points behind Verstappen in second and just one point ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton in fourth.
